title: Rollout Ops Playbook: Mini Rituals and Annotated Calendar
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-focused playbook for the upcoming weeklong rollout (canary -> regional -> global). It's intentionally lightweight: a set of recurring micro-rituals (what we do on the hour/day), an annotated calendar with signal owners, and a first-pass release-notes draft to share with PMs and SRE. Use for last-minute run-throughs and as a live working doc during on-call windows.

Summary of rollout plan (high level):
- Phase 0 (canary): 2027-03-16 09:00 UTC start, 2% traffic, telemetry 30m cadence
- Phase 1 (regional ramp): 2027-03-16 13:00 UTC start, 10% traffic, regional splits applied, 15m cadence
- Phase 2 (global roll): 2027-03-17 00:00 UTC start, progressive ramp to 100% over 6 hours, emergency freeze window 02:00-04:00 UTC
- Post-roll validation and sampling: 2027-03-17 06:00-18:00 UTC (slo/sla checks and sample prompts)

Quick operator rituals (do these on every cadence):
- On-card check (5m): confirm runbook open, channel #release-runbook pinned, on-call present
- Telemetry snapshot (2m): main dashboard open, top-3 KPIs visible: p50 latency, p99 latency, error-rate
- Dry smoke test (3m): run 3 golden prompts from /eval/golden-set and confirm semantic match >= threshold
- Rollback readiness (1m): ensure rollback toggle is accessible, last-green commit id noted

Annotated calendar (timezone: UTC) - owner initials in parens
- 2027-03-16 08:00 — Preflight standup (AK, MS, PN) — quick checklist, confirm infra warm pools, token buckets
- 2027-03-16 09:00 — Canary lift (AK) — 2% traffic -> monitor first 30m for errors and latency spikes
- 2027-03-16 09:30 — Canary validation pulse (EC) — run automated smoke suite + manual sample review
- 2027-03-16 11:00 — Telemetry deep-dive (MS) — look at model routing ratios, KV cache hit-rate, GPU queue length
- 2027-03-16 13:00 — Regional ramp start (PN) — 10% per-region; stagger region start times by 10m to detect locality regressions
- 2027-03-16 14:00 — Canary-to-regional crosscheck (AK) — validate metrics parity vs canary baseline
- 2027-03-16 18:00 — Holdpoint sync (AK, MS, PN) — go/no-go for global roll window
- 2027-03-17 00:00 — Global progressive ramp (EC) — multi-stage increments: 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% (45m between steps)
- 2027-03-17 06:00 — Post-roll sanity (AK) — sampling and quality evals, trigger alert if semantic delta > 2%
- 2027-03-17 12:00 — Ops retrospective quick (all) — capture immediate observations; detailed retro to follow

Signal thresholds and owners (fast reference):
- Error-rate >= 0.5% sustained for 10m -> Paging (SRE on-call)
- p99 latency increase > 2x baseline over 10m -> Investigate (Performance lead)
- Semantic regression (eval set) delta > 1.5% -> Pause ramp and A/B analysis (Applied ML)
- KV cache miss-rate > 25% -> Rollback quantization/compile flags (Serving runtime)
- Cost spike: token spend per-minute > 2x expected -> Throttle non-critical routes (Platform)

Rollback matrix (quick):
- Fast rollback (automated): flip traffic switch to last-known-good model variant (T-0 < 5m)
- Targeted rollback: regional rollback to previous model for impacted region(s) (T-0 ~ 10-30m)
- Emergency platform rollback: revert infra change and bounce serving pool (requires SRE lead)

Preflight checklist (to tick before 09:00 canary start):
[ ] Feature flags created and validated in staging
[ ] Canary config baked into routing policy and verified via /admin/route-sim
[ ] Smoke tests green on staging and dry-run against canary infra
[ ] Quota/burst limits reviewed and increased for carve-out if needed
[ ] Observability dashboards pinned and saved (link to dashboard list below)
[ ] On-call rotation and escalation path confirmed in Slack

Live observations (notes for running doc):
- Note to self: keep the golden prompts list small (3-5) and rotating each week to avoid overfitting cache artifacts
- If we see regional semantic drift but stable latency, consider targeted decoder config tweak rather than global rollback
- Watch model-variant routing for fallback loops (rare bug where fallback cascades and amplifies latency)

Release notes draft (shareable with PMs, first-pass):
Title: "March 2027: Serving runtime and routing optimizations — staged rollout"
Overview:
- Deploys a new compilation profile that favors reduced p99 by ~10% on long-sequence workloads. Includes an updated fallback policy for regional overloads and a conservative KV cache warmup routine.
Changes:
- Serving runtime: kernel selection heuristics updated to prefer tiled-attn when sequence length > 1024 (PR #612)
- Routing: added per-region prefailure thresholds and more granular canary routing controls (JIRA RE-1987)
- Observability: new trace spans for request batching and cache fill events
Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: potential p50 regression for short prompt workloads during initial warming. Mitigation: conservative canary percentage and staged region ramp.
- Risk: increased throttle events under synthetic load. Mitigation: temporarily raised burst buckets for monitored lanes and rapid rollback plan.
Known issues:
- Minor: debug logging in one test shard still enabled (will be stripped in next patch)

Post-deploy checks (first 48h):
- Run daily condensed eval run at 09:00 UTC (automated) and compare against baseline tags
- Sample 50 human prompts from callouts channel and spot-check for hallucination rate
- Cost monitoring: token/minute trend line analysis for each major customer route

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide on warmpool size for EU-west (MS to propose numbers by 2027-03-12)
- Should we disable some diagnostic traces for the heavy tail by default? (PN owns decision)
- Add an automated smoke that runs rollback path periodically (follow-up ticket?)

Appendix (links and quick commands):
- Smoke runner: infra/tools/smoke-runner --env=canary --set=golden-set-A
- Route sim: /admin/route-sim?target=canary
- Dashboards: confluence.redwood.internal/display/RE/rollout-dashboards (bookmark this)
- Slack: #release-runbook for coordination, @sre-oncall for paging

Endnotes:
This is intentionally terse — use as the single source during active rollout windows. I'll expand into the longer-run postmortem notebook after the 72h observation window.
